title: Orbit release timetable and degassing notes
content:
Purpose: informal working notes for a low-risk, phased release that I can iterate on. Using an ‘orbit’ metaphor — small tight loop early, widen rings once heat is proven. Focus: version-lock strategy, warm cohorts, escape hatches, and quick health checks to avoid noisy rollbacks.

High-level goals:
- Avoid customer-visible errors during model flips and config changes.
- Verify latency tail and error-rate behavior on realistic traffic slices.
- Provide a fast path to revert (<= 3 min) and a slower mitigation path for partial disruptions.
- Capture minimal telemetry to make go/no-go decisions in first 30 minutes of each ring.

Definitions (quick):
- version-lock: explicit routing to a specific model+quantization image. Use for tenants that opt-in.
- staging-cohort: internal test traffic (non-customer) from canaries, bots.
- ring-1..n: progressive traffic buckets, each 10–25% depending on risk appetite.
- degassing: gradual reduction of implicit risk (cooling off noisy metrics) before expanding rings.

Preflight checklist (do not skip):
- Confirm control-plane snapshot contains both old and new version-lock manifests. (GH PR + release tag)
- Smoke test: headless end-to-end with synthetic prompts (3x) across seq lengths [32, 256, 1024].
- KV cache priming: run 200 warmup requests with typical prompt prefixes for top 10 tenants.
- Nightly infra window: ensure no infra deployments for 90 min around orbit.
- Alert ownership: assign 2 responders and 1 TL for first 60 minutes.

Timetable (suggested, adjustable):
- T0 -30m: preflight checklist pass, start logging extra debug headers (X-ORBIT-ID, X-WARM-COHORT).
- T0 -10m: route 0.5% production to ring-1 via edge shadow toggle (keeps client opaque).
- T0: open ring-1 to 2% production (select low-risk tenants, version-lock optional).
- T0 +15m: evaluate 5m and 15m windows (p95 latency, 5xx count, avg token time).
- T0 +40m: if stable, expand to ring-2 (10–15%). Continue degassing for 30–60m between rings.
- T0 +4h: full ramp target (50–100%) depending on degradation profile and business hours.

Quick go/no-go heuristics (first 30m):
- Immediate STOP if: sustained 5xx increase > 2x baseline AND incident affects >1% of traffic or critical tenants.
- Pause and degas if: p95 latency > baseline + 150ms for 15 min OR user-visible failures for non-internal cohorts.
- Continue if: p95 <= baseline + 50ms and no tail spikes, 5xx within <20% of baseline.

Version-lock considerations:
- Prefer explicit version-lock for enterprise tenants for first orbit (they can opt-in).
- If using rolling image labels (latest), ensure fallback tag is immutable and tested (image:sha).
- Keep mapping table in control plane to allow one-line flip back: route model -> old-image:sha.

Observability quicklist (striped, minimal):
- p50/p95/p99 token latency by model variant and by tenant.
- Error rate by code (4xx vs 5xx) and by handler (router vs runtime).
- Memory/GPU saturation per host and KV cache hit ratio.
- Request histograms bucketed by sequence length and prompt template.
- One lightweight synthetic canary that pings every 10s and posts to /deploy-health.

Escape hatches and recovery paths:
- Fast rollback: single control-plane mapping flip to old-image:sha + CDN edge invalidation (estimate 2–3m).
- Soft diversion: divert traffic to a cheaper smaller model variant in same family (re-route policy).
- Partial pin: move high-value tenants back to old-image while leaving rest on new image.
- Grounding: if storage or infra issue, pause all new sessions and allow in-flight to finish.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need a canonical small probe set for KV priming (SLA and prefix coverage). Who owns this? Jill?
- Evaluate adding a short-lived trace-id that surfaces in logs and request headers for first 60m.
- Would like an automated degas timer that enforces minimum hold between rings (avoid manual drift).

Post-mortem trigger thresholds (auto):
- Any rollback that is not a single control-plane flip AND took > 15 min to remediate.
- Any customer-visible regression detected for an SLA-tier customer.

Actions (next edits):
- Convert heuristics into a small checklist card for on-call (1 pager).
- Wire a lightweight GH action to emit the preflight smoke results as a comment on the PR.
- Draft a tiny runbook snippet for version-lock flips (1–2 commands).

If anything goes sideways during the first orbit, prefer conservative decant (move traffic back slowly) vs aggressive rollback — preserves telemetry and helps root-cause.

-- Rohan
